files.role: Public frozen V1 module facade and physical-column projection/mapping helpers. Declares encoding, format, page_table, reader and writer; maps core Field/Schema trees to shared ReaderProjection without IO or modern metadata grammar.
files.limits: All physical lines of this file were read during ANALYZE60. Tests were inspected, not executed. Source remains read-only and offline; no build, test, benchmark, fixture generation or dependency installation was run. Frozen V1 behavior is recorded for compatibility, not proposed as the basis for new features. Concrete V1 codecs, reader/writer lifecycle and statistics remain pending whole-file analysis; narrow caller/helper context is recorded separately. Arithmetic, malformed-input, allocation and cancellation consequences are source-level observations, not executed reproductions. No unsafe block or global mutable state is declared in this file.
ranges: SPDX and module documentation identify the canonical V1 reader/writer/metadata/page-table home, historical accepted footer identities(0,0..=2) and emitted(0,2). Those numbers are a declared contract here; exact version parsing/constants and writer call sites are elsewhere. Five child modules are public. BTreeMap, Arc, core Field/Schema/Result and shared ReaderProjection are the local dependencies.

Private append_field_ids walks supplied fields preorder. Cast each signed field.id to u32, append a mapped column if present, silently skip an unmapped node, then recurse into children unless the node is Blob or packed struct. A missing parent does not block ordinary children. Supplied map values are neither bounds-checked nor deduplicated; negative IDs wrap to u32. Blob/packed descendants never contribute separately.

Public projection_from_field_ids allocates an index vector, uses the above traversal, and clones the supplied Schema into a fresh Arc. This follows the derived Clone implementations of Schema, Field and Dictionary; loaded dictionary ArrayRef members retain shared array storage, so this is not a promise to copy all backing data (rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/schema.rs:24-31; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes/field.rs:134-161; rust/lance-core/src/datatypes.rs:561-568). It returns ReaderProjection directly, even for empty schema/indices, absent mappings or repeated physical values. It preserves the full supplied schema rather than removing unmapped fields; validation is a consumer responsibility. No IO or fallible Result.

projection_from_whole_schema builds the private full-schema ID-to-column map, then applies the same projection helper. Map creation uses two temporary vectors and a BTreeMap; duplicated field IDs collapse to the last assigned column in the map and may be repeated again in traversal. This is not a one-to-one mapping validator.

projection_from_column_names builds physical mapping from the original full schema before calling Schema::project. Projection errors propagate; otherwise compute indices from projected preorder using original physical columns. It does not renumber the selected subset or validate uniqueness/bounds beyond delegated schema projection.

physical_column_count returns1 for any Blob or packed struct without visiting descendants; otherwise returns1 plus recursive child counts. Ordinary struct/container parents count even when they have no data page. Addition/sum are unchecked usize arithmetic; recursive depth is not bounded.

data_file_columns creates parallel Vec<i32> IDs/indices and calls private preorder appender with a temporary counter0. Empty schema yields two empty vectors. Field IDs remain their original signed values, while physical indices are assigned consecutively.

Private field_id_to_column_index zips the parallel vectors, casts both sides to u32 and collects BTreeMap. Duplicate IDs overwrite earlier entries; negative IDs/overflowed signed columns are not rejected. The map is only a projection helper, not persisted itself here.

append_physical_fields emits every visited node ID and current physical counter before ordinary i32 increment and recursive descent. Blob/packed struct stop recursion; other parent/child nodes each occupy a slot. No overflow, duplicate-ID, negative-ID or schema validation. File ends without a local test module; compatibility/projection tests in other analyzed files do not constitute exhaustive edge-case coverage of these helpers.
